subject: Veridian Health — Renewal capacity plan & GPU sizing runbook
messages:
From: Sara Lindquist <sara.lindquist@veridianhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Veridian Procurement <procurement@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal ahead — sizing guidance request

Hi Markus,

Our Dedicated capacity renewal is coming up in late September and we're seeing higher-than-expected tail usage on our inference fleet. Q2 utilization reports show a 95th percentile sustained concurrent GPU usage of ~22 A100-equivalents and frequent short spikes to ~30 during batch jobs. We currently have a 32-GPU dedicated pool with documented burst credits for up to 48 GPUs.

We'd like a recommended sizing plan for the renewal that:
- keeps latency SLOs for production chat endpoints,
- reduces per-token cost where possible,
- and provides a path to cover peak batch windows without frequent throttling.

Can you advise on the trade-offs for adding reserved GPUs vs keeping burst capacity, and share an initial runbook and estimate? Attaching our utilization export as requested.

Thanks,
Sara Lindquist
Head of Platform, Veridian Health
[sent from mobile]

Attachment: utilization_report_q2.csv (CSV - 245 KB)

Plan: I'd like to run a short tech alignment with our SEs to convert those signals into a practical sizing recommendation (reserved GPUs, burst sizing, and autoscale thresholds). Can you do a 30-min call tomorrow (Tue) 10:00–10:30 PT? If so, I'll bring the runbook and a first-pass cost delta.

If call doesn't work, we'll send a written runbook with three options (conservative reserved add, hybrid reserved+burst conversion, and aggressive reserved buydown) and clear impact on unit economics.

Best,

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Veridian renewal — sizing runbook (first pass)

Team — copying the Q2 export Sara sent. High level summary and recommendation below; want your feedback before I send to customer.

Summary of signals (from Veridian export):
- Dedicated pool: 32 x A100-equivalent GPUs.
- Observed 95th percentile concurrent usage (prod inference): ~22 GPUs sustained over daily windows.
- Typical nightly batch windows cause spikes to 28–32 GPUs for 1–3 hours, twice/week.
- Token mix: 70% short-turn chat (<64 tokens), 30% longer rerank/batch (avg 800 tokens).

Design goals: maintain sub-200ms median latency for chat endpoints, eliminate throttling during batch windows, and reduce cost by shifting steady-state to reserved capacity where viable.

Options (first pass):
1) Conservative reserved add (low friction)
   - Add +8 reserved GPUs (target pool 40).
   - Keep burst credits to cover spikes to 48.
   - Expected outcome: removes routine throttling, modest incremental monthly cost (+25–30% vs current).

2) Hybrid conversion (recommended)
   - Convert 12 of the current burst credit equivalent into reserved (effective: reserved 44, burst available to 60 but with smaller credit burn).
   - Add +4 reserved GPUs staged (week 0 +4, week 4 +4) for runway.
   - Update autoscale: lower latency SLO weight, aggressive prefix caching for chat, and batch scheduling for off-peak hours.
   - Expected outcome: better unit economics (estimated 12–18% cost reduction over pure burst model) and smoother tail handling.

3) Aggressive reserved buydown (higher commitment)
   - Commit to 48 reserved GPUs (no burst).
   - Requires redistribution of batch jobs to daytime pools or temporary batch throttling.
   - Expected outcome: best per-unit cost but requires org changes (batch scheduling) and longer negotiation.

Operational runbook (short):
- Week 0: finalize SOW and pricing; provision +4 reserved GPUs as soft buffer; enable higher KV cache TTL for chat model; start token-level cost tracking.
- Week 2: monitor 95th/99th percentile signals; if tail still causes >5% throttling, provision additional +4 reserved GPUs (week 4).
- Week 4–6: convert agreed number of burst credits to reserved (if hybrid path chosen).
- Post-renewal (30–60d): validate QoE with Canary users, keep fallback routing to smaller-chat model for non-critical traffic.

Risks & mitigations:
- Large batch windows cause short, heavy spikes -> schedule batch runs in a prioritized queue and backfill during low-latency windows.
- Unexpected growth -> can enable short-term burst increments but will need a tranche commitment for long-term stability.

Pricing delta (rough):
- Option 1: +25–30% monthly spend.
- Option 2 (hybrid): +10–15% monthly, with projected 12% unit-cost improvement after 60d due to caching and staging.
- Option 3: +5–8% monthly but requires organizational batch changes.

Attachments: I plan to attach a short runbook spreadsheet with the staged timeline and a draft SOW. Thoughts?

—Markus

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Veridian renewal — sizing runbook (first pass)

Markus / team — short notes:
- Agree with hybrid as the pragmatic default. Customer prefers fewer surprise costs.
- SE notes: make sure autoscaler has a conservative cooldown for batch job terminations and expose a burst budget report in the Console.
- Ops: recommend pre-warming 2 GPUs with heavier KV cache for chat model so tail cold-starts are less frequent.

Happy for me to draft the technical appendix for the runbook (autoscale knobs, cache TTLs, cost delta per token).

—Ben

Subject: Veridian renewal — proposal and next steps

Hi Sara & team — thanks for the call earlier this week. Per our discussion, attached is a concise runbook and a draft SOW with three options so you can pick the runway that matches your internal tolerance for commitment vs flexibility.

Key recommendation (hybrid, summary):
- Start with +4 reserved GPUs provisioned immediately on contract renewal, convert 12 burst-equivalent credits into reserved over a 30–60 day window, and keep a 16-GPU burst buffer for rare batch spikes.
- Adjust autoscale policy: 3-min cooldown for scale-down during batch-run windows; pre-warm 2 GPUs with extended KV cache for chat to reduce cold-start latency.
- Monitoring: we will enable a dedicated dashboard (token-level cost, 95th/99th concurrent usage, burst credit burn rate) and a weekly runbook review for the first 8 weeks.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: sign attached SOW_draft_v2.pdf and confirm start date (we proposed 2026-09-01 to align with your renewal).
2) Technical: Ben will send the technical appendix and Priyom will confirm autoscale knobs (ETA 48 hours).
3) Commercial: I’ll provide an updated pricing table showing month-to-month delta between options.

Attachments: veridian_renewal_runbook.xlsx (runbook, timeline), SOW_draft_v2.pdf (draft SOW), utilization_report_q2.csv (customer-supplied).

If you'd like, we can also run a short cost-sensitivity model against your historical token mix (takes ~24 hours).

Thanks and talk soon,
